finding: THE v1 TASK SET HAS NO LOCALISATION PROBLEM: 10 symptom strings, each mapping to exactly one bug region, over 2,000 tasks. A ten-row lookup table localises at 100%.
how_it_surfaced: G's read-only head scored 100.0% on held-out slices at BOTH layers 18 and 27. The permutation control passed (shuffled training labels -> 24%, chance), so it was not a fitting artefact -- which is exactly what made it worth chasing rather than celebrating. It survived PCA to 8 dimensions and a training set of 100 examples, both at 100%. A signal that needs 8 dimensions and 100 examples is not a learned readout of a hard quantity; it is a key being copied. The FIRST decision prompt contains NO PROGRAM TEXT AT ALL -- only the symptom line, the four region names and the budget -- so the state had nothing else to read.

what_it_invalidates.G (read-only controller head): untestable on v1. There is no localisation decision to make, so a head that chooses well proves nothing about activations.
what_it_invalidates.the agent's 88.05% first-hypothesis accu: is BELOW a ten-row lookup table on a string the prompt hands it. The 478 misses are not a capability gap in localisation; they are the model declining to use a deterministic key.
what_it_invalidates.the localisation headroom in every G pla: was never headroom. 理's ceiling argument and my own repair-floor decomposition were both computed over a quantity the task set gives away.

what_it_does_NOT_invalidate.A / C / F cost results: those compared COST at held capability and never depended on localisation being hard.
what_it_does_NOT_invalidate.the repair floor: ~25% of episodes localise and still fail -- if anything this strengthens it, because localisation was even cheaper than we thought and the episodes still failed.
what_it_does_NOT_invalidate.G-trivial's -36.2: it measured what OVERRIDING a chooser costs, which is a fact about the agent loop, not about the task set's difficulty. Its symptom!=bug collapse stands.

bounds: v1 only. tasks/v0 and tasks/heldout_v0 NOT checked by this script.

The key is the FULL symptom string including the FAIL/ERROR prefix: 'FAIL: test_report_all_items' -> producer but 'ERROR: test_report_all_items' -> consumer. A reader who keys on the test name alone gets 2 of 10 rows wrong.
This says the MAPPING is deterministic. It does not say the model USES it -- the agent sits at 88.05%, so it plainly does not.
